learn.title: Rows and columns
learn.body: A two-dimensional array is a grid. `int g[2][3];` has 2 rows and 3 columns. You pick an element with two indexes, `g[row][col]`, and both start at 0.

learn.title: Fill a grid
learn.body: Braces inside braces give one row each. Here `g[1][2]` is the last element, 6, and `g[0][1]` is 2.

learn.title: Two loops
learn.body: The outer loop picks the row, the inner loop walks along it. It prints two lines, each with three numbers.

learn.title: Stored row by row
learn.body: In memory the rows sit one after another: 1 2 3 4 5 6. So `g[1][0]` comes right after `g[0][2]`. Because of this, a function must be told the number of columns.

learn.title: Passing a grid
learn.body: Write `void show(int g[][3], int rows)`. The column count must be given, the row count may be left out. The function needs the width to know where each row starts.

learn.title: A tic-tac-toe board
learn.body: Use `char b[3][3]` with the rows X O X, blank X O, and O blank X.
steps: In a loop that is `b[i][i]` for `i` from 0 to 2
All three are `X`, so X wins on the diagonal

questions.prompt: In `int g[2][3];`, how many elements are there?

questions.explanation: The first index picks the row, the second the column.

questions.prompt: In `{{1, 2, 3}, {4, 5, 6}}`, what is `g[1][0]`? Type the number.
questions.explanation: Row 1 is `{4, 5, 6}` and its first element is 4.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of row 1, `{4, 5, 6}`? Type the number.
A function that takes `int g[][3]` must be told the number of \_\_ in the type.
questions.explanation: The width tells the function where each row starts.

questions.prompt: To visit every element, how do you usually loop?
choices: A single loop with no index
questions.explanation: The outer loop walks rows, the inner loop walks the columns of that row.

questions.prompt: Match each tic-tac-toe expression to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Row first, then column, both from 0.

questions.prompt: Put the order in which the nested loops print `g[0][0]` to `g[1][2]`.
questions.explanation: The inner loop finishes a whole row before the outer loop moves on.
